aspects.says: getDeclaredFields() lists one class's own fields, private ones included; a superclass's private fields are listed by its own Class, and getFields() returns only public ones.
basis: section:setAccessible Opens Private Members of Class-Path Code, Not of the JDK

aspects.says: Nested classes and their outer class use each other's private members; since Java 11 the JVM knows them as nestmates instead of going through generated access methods.
basis: section:Private Is Checked per Class, Not per Object
aspects.reason: a compile-time permission with nothing for a wrong solution to do differently at run time; the bridge methods show only in javap output

aspects.says: An override may widen access but never narrow it, so widening a protected hook to public in a library breaks every subclass that overrides it as protected.
basis: section:An Override May Widen Access but Never Narrow It

aspects.says: On the class path any jar can declare classes in a package and use its package-private members (unless the jar is sealed); the module path refuses two modules with the same package.
basis: section:No Modifier Means Package-Private, and a Subclass in Another Package Can't Override It
aspects.reason: it needs two jars and a module-path launch, while a practice builds one source tree on the class path

aspects.says: A package-private method is not overridden by a same-signature method in a subclass in another package; the base class keeps calling its own, silently, and @Override turns that into a compile error.
basis: section:No Modifier Means Package-Private, and a Subclass in Another Package Can't Override It

aspects.says: private is checked per class, not per object: code in a class can read and write the private fields of any instance of that class, so it bypasses that instance's own checks unless it goes through its methods.
basis: section:Private Is Checked per Class, Not per Object

aspects.says: protected is wider than package-private: every class of the declaring package can use the member, subclass or not.
basis: section:Protected Opens the Package, and Other Packages Only Through the Subclass's Own Type
aspects.reason: a compile-time permission: a practice in one package cannot show a wrong solution that compiles and behaves differently

aspects.says: Outside the declaring package a subclass reaches a protected instance member only through an expression of its own type or a subtype, never through a reference of the base type.
basis: section:Protected Opens the Package, and Other Packages Only Through the Subclass's Own Type

aspects.says: setAccessible(true) opens private members of class-path code but throws the unchecked InaccessibleObjectException on JDK internals unless the package is opened; trySetAccessible() answers false instead.
basis: section:setAccessible Opens Private Members of Class-Path Code, Not of the JDK
